Assistant A provides a correct divide-and-conquer algorithm for finding the median of two sorted arrays. The logic properly handles both odd and even total lengths and correctly identifies the k-th smallest element by eliminating half of the remaining candidates at each step. While the provided Python code uses list slicing (which technically uses O(n) auxiliary space) and recursion (O(log n) stack space), the underlying algorithm can be trivially converted to O(1) space by passing indices instead of slicing, and its time complexity of O(log n) satisfies the O(n) requirement. In contrast, Assistant B's code is algorithmically incorrect—it crashes on basic inputs (e.g., index out of bounds), does not compute the median (fails to handle even/odd cases or averaging), and its pointer logic does not solve the problem. Therefore, Assistant A's response is significantly more helpful, relevant, and accurate.
